Title: PostDoc - Uncertainty-Aware Optimization in Inverse Problems for Next-Generation 3D Scanning
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
3Shape and DTU Compute (Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science at the Technical University of Denmark) invite applications for an Industrial Postdoctoral position partially funded by Innovation Fund Denmark. The position is a 2-year fixed-term appointment starting in January 2027 (small variations in the start date may be possible depending on the candidate’s preference).




The project addresses a fundamental challenge in computational imaging and large-scale optimization: how can uncertainty in measurements be quantified, propagated, and ultimately leveraged to improve the reliability of reconstructed 3d models?




Modern 3D scanning systems rely on advanced optimization algorithms to reconstruct geometry and color from large volumes of sensor data. While these algorithms produce highly accurate results, they typically provide limited information about the confidence and uncertainty associated with the reconstructed output. Developing methods that can efficiently estimate and propagate uncertainty in the input data through large-scale iterative optimization algorithms has the potential to improve reconstruction quality, enable more informed algorithmic decisions, and support the next generation of intelligent scanning systems.




The successful candidate will conduct research at the intersection of numerical linear algebra, optimization, uncertainty quantification, and computational imaging. The project will investigate: (i) how to characterize measurement uncertainty, (ii) how uncertainty propagates through iterative solvers, (iii) how to develop new mathematical frameworks for uncertainty-aware optimization, and (iv) how to validate the proposed methods through simulations and deployment in medical 3D reconstruction algorithms developed at 3Shape.




The position offers a unique opportunity to combine fundamental research with industrial impact. Working closely with leading researchers at DTU and engineers at 3Shape, the candidate will contribute to scientific publications, software prototype development, and innovation activities aimed at strengthening the theoretical foundations and practical performance of future 3D scanning technologies.




About us

At 3Shape we aim to advance dental treatment and diagnostics with advanced software and 3D scanners designed for dental professionals across the globe. Our purpose is to advance innovation in dentistry, continuously enhancing patient care and outcomes.




This role places you at the heart of our technological advancements within Product Creation, namely TRIOS & SCANNER SW, offering the chance to shape the trajectory of our innovative products and software applications.




About the project

The project is a 2-year project between 3Shape and the Technical University of Denmark, partly funded by Innovation Fund Denmark. The academic co-supervisor will be Professor Per Christian Hansen at DTU Compute (Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science).




The research focuses on uncertainty-aware methods for large-scale linear least squares problems, which form the mathematical backbone of many inverse problems and optimization tasks in 3D reconstruction. The objective is to develop new theoretical and computational tools for quantifying and propagating uncertainty through iterative solution methods, and to translate these developments into practical algorithms for medical 3D reconstruction systems.




What You’ll Do

In this role, you will contribute both to the theoretical foundation and the practical implementation of next-generation uncertainty-aware reconstruction algorithms. The work spans mathematical modelling, algorithm design, and software development in a medical imaging 3D reconstruction.

You will:

Develop methods for characterizing measurement uncertainty in medical 3D scanning data, including data-driven approaches and machine learning methods where appropriate, to obtain realistic and application-relevant uncertainty models.
Work hands-on with numerical algorithms, including iterative methods such as Krylov subspace methods and related solvers.
Develop and analyse new methods for uncertainty-aware linear least squares optimization, with a focus on large-scale iterative solvers.
Design mathematical frameworks for quantifying how uncertainty evolves through optimization algorithms used in 3D reconstruction.
Contribute to the architectural design of uncertainty-aware components within existing reconstruction pipelines.
Translate theoretical models into efficient, scalable implementations suitable for industrial use.
Design and run simulation studies to validate theoretical developments under realistic conditions.
Collaborate with researchers and engineers to integrate new methods into production-oriented 3D scanning systems.
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, technical reports, and potential patentable innovations.




What We’re Looking For

A PhD in Mathematics, Statistics, or a related discipline. The PhD must have been awarded after March 2021 (or will be obtained within November 2026).
Strong expertise in numerical linear algebra, optimization, and/or inverse problems.
Solid understanding of linear least squares methods and iterative solvers, ideally methods based on Krylov subspace methods.
Experience with or strong interest in uncertainty quantification, statistical modelling, or probabilistic methods.
Strong programming skills in at least one programming language (ideally two), such as C#, C++, or Python.
Familiarity with machine learning methods is an advantage, particularly for data-driven modelling of complex systems.
Ability to work independently and take ownership of research problems while also contributing to a collaborative industrial-academic environment.
Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex mathematical ideas clearly in both academic and applied settings.




What 3Shape offers

A vibrant and international environment with social, diverse, and highly skilled and collaborative colleagues - we are more than 50 nationalities in our DK based office
Breakfast every day, and delicious and healthy lunch cooked by our private chefs.
We provide a great social work environment with many optional activities and social clubs, ranging from wine & beer, board games, running to bicycle clubs.
Good work/life balance.
Attractive offices and R&D lab spaces in downtown Copenhagen close to Kgs. Nytorv, Nyhavn, and the Copenhagen Canals.
Purpose: Endeavor to improve dental patients on a global scale.




Staying true to our values and D&I efforts, we encourage all relevant applicants to apply, and we ask you NOT to add any photos or sensitive information (age, marital status, nationality) during the application process.




We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

AI is moving from prototypes to production-ready solutions. The engineers who can take it there matter more than ever.

At Heyra, we build operational AI: systems, workflows, and data platforms that live in production from day one. We work with companies that are moving quickly and need solutions that improve the way they operate.

We're looking for an AI Engineer who is as comfortable in the code as in the data underneath it. Someone who can design, build, and ship AI solutions today, and grow into setting technical direction as the company grows.

On smaller engagements, you may be the only engineer on the project, which means owning it from problem to production yourself. Translating business needs into AI solutions that actually ship
Integrating scalable AI systems through APIs and cloud environments

Title: AI/ML Scientist — Medical Imaging
Description:
AI/ML Scientist — Medical Imaging

Copenhagen · Permanent · Presented by Black Swans Exist




The short version

A venture-backed Danish medical imaging company is hiring its first dedicated AI/ML scientist. The company has a CE-marked product already in clinical use and is now building the next generation of diagnostic tools on top of the imaging data that product generates.

This is not a role where you inherit a dataset and a backlog. The data largely does not exist yet. Part of this job is going out to hospitals, working alongside clinicians, and finding out whether the data they hold actually contains the answer to the question they are asking. The other part is turning that into methods and working prototypes.

If you want a clean pipeline and a defined problem, this is the wrong role. If you want to define the problem, it is close to ideal.




The company

Venture-backed, Danish, around 40 people, with offices in Copenhagen. The technology is PET-based functional imaging that produces quantitative measurements rather than pictures alone — the ability to put a number on physiological function, not just describe what an image looks like.

The first product is CE-marked and in clinical use, with a pivotal trial running and a regulatory submission planned in the United States. Quantification is the core of the company's value: it is what competitors do not offer, and it is the thing this role is hired to extend.

The company is named at first conversation. We have not put it in writing here.




The mission

The imaging data is the future product line. Today the company measures blood flow in the heart. The question is what else the same data can answer - in cardiology, in neurology, and beyond - and what methods are needed to get there.




You are hired to answer that. You will be the company's dedicated AI/ML voice, joining a software team of eight and reporting to the Head of Software. You will work across R&D, clinical development, quality and regulatory.




Concretely, the first twelve months look like this:

Building working relationships with clinicians and technicians at partner hospitals, in Denmark and nearby
Getting into clinics and understanding how the scans are actually acquired and read
Identifying which data holds real signal — and being honest when it does not
Running studies and projects alongside hospital doctors
Building prototypes that show whether a method works

Success at six months is measured in relationships and prototypes, not in shipped features.




What you will actually do

Invent, prototype and mature algorithms for extracting clinically meaningful information from PET data
Translate clinical and scientific questions into testable algorithmic solutions
Build the pipelines around the work — acquisition, quality control, processing, visualization, presentation of findings
Go to hospitals. Observe workflows. Ask clinicians what they need and validate that your assumptions survive contact with clinical reality
Evaluate emerging methods and tools, and shape which directions the company invests in
Support the AI/ML dimension of medical device compliance as methods mature toward product — CE-marking and FDA

Travel is roughly two to three days per month, primarily within Denmark and southern Sweden.




Who we are looking for

Essential

Demonstrable AI/ML development experience — applied, and with something you can point to and say "I built that"
A software engineering and algorithm background, hands-on with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX or Keras, and disciplined about testing and version control
Experience with data collection, selection, integration and quality control, and preparing datasets for training
Comfort starting from a rough idea rather than a specification
Someone who wants to be in the room with clinicians. This role does not work from a desk — you need to be willing to initiate conversations with doctors and technicians, ask uncomfortable questions, and keep asking
Roughly three to eight years of relevant experience. A PhD, or a PhD plus postdoc, counts — provided the work was applied and you have built things

Strongly preferred

Medical imaging: DICOM, and work on 3D or 4D volumetric data — segmentation, registration, classification or quantification. PET, MR or X-ray all count
PET-specific knowledge — reconstruction, attenuation and scatter correction, tracer kinetics, quantification. Genuinely valuable, genuinely not required on day one. The company expects to teach this
Medical device software or SaMD experience — IEC 62304, quality systems, verification and validation, CE-marking or FDA
A background in healthcare, medtech, diagnostics or another regulated field




Education

Computer science, biomedical engineering, medical physics or similar is typical. Proven capability substitutes for credentials.




Relocation

Candidates relocating to Denmark will be considered.




What this is, honestly

The genuine appeal. This is the company's first and only AI/ML hire. Nobody has done this before you, there is no established way of working to inherit, and the direction the company takes on AI is the direction you argue for. It is an unusual amount of ownership for someone at this level, and it is the main reason to take the role.




What you should weigh. You will be the only AI/ML person among eight developers. There is no in-house peer to review your methods and no senior imaging-AI person to learn from — the clinical and scientific expertise sits with the company's hospital collaborators and advisors rather than inside the building. Some people find that liberating. Others find it isolating, and it is worth being honest with yourself about which you are before you apply.

The other thing to weigh is the data. It is early. Expect to spend real time on access, agreements, site visits and data quality before you spend it on model architecture.




Interested, or want to know more?

Black Swans Exist is running this search exclusively. We will tell you who the company is at first conversation, and we will tell you the parts that are not in this document.

If it is not right for you but you know who it is right for, we would genuinely like to hear from you.

Data science

Title: Consultant for Data Science Consultancy Team
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
At Annalect, we help businesses across industries make better decisions — from marketing strategies to business development and sales forecasting. Our approach combines deep industry understanding with advanced, AI-powered analytical methods, enabling us to deliver insights and recommendations that make a real difference for our clients. In Denmark, we are more than 70 specialists based in Copenhagen and Aarhus. As part of Omnicom Media Group, we have over 300 colleagues in Denmark and a global network of more than 5,000 experts with whom we collaborate to create the best possible solutions for our clients.




Consultant for Data Science Consultancy Team

Are you passionate about applying Data Science in real-world scenarios? Do you want to leverage mathematics, statistics, and programming to help our clients make better decisions? Are you driven by data and analysis, and eager to translate insights into actionable recommendations? Join Annalect’s Data Science Consultancy team!




About the Role

We are looking for a new colleague to join Annalect, Omnicom Media Group’s specialist unit for data-driven analytics and decision support systems. Our work includes analyses that quantify the impact of our clients’ marketing activities and provide the foundation for ongoing optimization. Annalect consists of 60 employees, with 20 dedicated to the Data Science Consultancy team. Our team utilizes mathematics, statistics, and econometrics to process large volumes of data, delivering business-oriented decision support. As a Data Science Consultant, you will be involved in the entire project lifecycle for our clients – from data collection and coding, to building and optimizing statistical models in R, and communicating results and recommendations to clients. You will work closely with a project lead and the team, receiving ongoing support and feedback. As you gain experience, you will have the opportunity to conduct analyses independently, manage client communications, and deliver your own projects.




Key Responsibilities:

Collect client data and extract data from media systems
Programming and data processing
Structure, code, and interpret data
Develop statistical models in R
Analyze results and prepare recommendations in close collaboration with a project lead
Prepare deliverables for clients in PowerPoint and dashboards
Maintain ongoing dialogue with clients and media agencies throughout the project
Lead your own projects




Your Profile

We imagine that you:

Hold a relevant academic degree (e.g., Cand.Merc. (MAT), Cand.polit. IMM, AEF, or similar)
Have basic experience with statistical models and methodologies
Possess strong analytical skills
Are proficient in R Studio (or other programming languages such as Python, SAS, VBA, SQL and are eager to further develop your skills in R Studio)
Are experienced in Excel and PowerPoint
Are interested in building an understanding of marketing, digital platforms, and the media landscape




What We Offer

We offer a position in an exciting company with many opportunities. You will be part of a strong professional community and work alongside some of the industry’s most talented specialists. We also have a vibrant social environment, including Friday bars, annual parties, company football team, DHL race, and more. Our culture is relaxed, with room for fun and focus for deep work on projects.




Interested?

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and reserve the right to close the posting once the right candidate has been found.

If you have any questions about the position or the company, please contact Analytics Director Anders Mousten at anders.mousten@omc.com.

Title: Senior Forward Deployed AI Scientist
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Job ID: 3090

Welcome to Group Technology, where we pride ourselves on engineering solutions that directly impact Nordea's 2030 goals to modernize data technology and accelerate AI.

We are looking for a skilled and collaborative Senior Forward Deployed AI Scientist to join our Forward Deployed AI team at Nordea. You will design and build scalable AI solutions, working closely with cross-functional teams to deliver agentic AI applications that drive value across the organization while ensuring ethical and sustainable development practices. 

Nordea is a place where traditions meet tomorrow. We are not just a bank; we are a tech employer on a mission to evolve finance securely and responsibly. Together, we impact millions of people's daily lives by ensuring they can access our solutions anytime, anywhere, while safeguarding their personal data and wealth. Join us in making an impact on the banking industry.

This position is a full-time, permanent role with hybrid working location based in Helsinki, Finland, Stockholm, Sweden, Gdańsk / Gdynia / Warsaw, Poland, or Copenhagen, Denmark. 

About Our Team   

Meet the Forward Deployed AI team. We are a collaborative and result-driven team working closely with every part of the bank to execute AI use cases. Our deep connections throughout Nordea and trusted reputation enable us to transform ambitious AI visions into practical, impactful solutions.

In this role, you will be embedded with the business areas, building strong partnerships and gaining deep domain expertise. This collaboration creates natural pathways for future career development, including potential transitions into business teams where your AI expertise will be highly valued. 

Main responsibilities in this role include, but are not limited to:


Design, develop, and scale transformative AI applications from concept to production to create technology that makes a real impact.
Translate ambiguous, open-ended business problems into well-defined machine learning problem statements in close collaboration with engineers and product teams.
Provide input to the full modeling lifecycle: problem framing, hypothesis formulation, model selection, experimentation, evaluation and iteration.
Develop and implement advanced machine learning models and agentic solutions for various business applications.
Explore emerging AI methods; share insights and build proofs of concept applicable to Nordea’s use cases.


Who You Are  

You will thrive in this role if you are excited to build AI solutions that solve real-world problems and drive meaningful change. You bring a growth mindset, collaborative problem-solving skills and excel at transforming complex technical concepts into clear solutions for both technical and non-technical audiences. 

We are looking for someone with most of the following experience and skills:  


BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering Physics, Data Science, Statistics, or equivalent practical experience
Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in Python, with minimum 3 years of hands-on experience developing and deploying AI/ML solutions in production environments
Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure or GCP), with a focus on deploying and operating AI/ML and data services at scale
Deep understanding of machine learning and statistics, with the ability to turn a business problem into a modelling one
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical teams and business stakeholders 
Excellent collaboration skills and experience working with diverse teams including data scientists, engineers, and product stakeholders


It would be ideal if you also have: 


Knowledge of agent testing methodologies, performance monitoring and maintaining agent reliability in production environments
Experience using agentic AI tools like Claude Code/Cowork, OpenAI Codex
Experience working in agile environments or tech-driven transformation projects
Familiarity with agent development frameworks and harnesses such as LangGraph, Deep Agents, AutoGen, CrewAI or similar, including multi-agent coordination and sub-agent delegation
Professional experience from working in regulated industries, e.g. banking, government, etc. 


We encourage applications from candidates who are passionate about AI and meet most of these criteria. We value diverse perspectives and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. 

If this sounds like you, get in touch!

Next steps

We kindly ask you to submit your application as soon as possible, but no later than 20/09/2026. Any applications or CVs sent by email, direct messages, or any other channel than our application forms, will not be accepted or considered.

At Nordea, we know that an inclusive workplace is a sustainable workplace. We deeply believe that our diverse backgrounds, experiences, characteristics, and traits make us better at serving our customers and communities.

Title: Quantitative Researcher - Equity Statistical Arbitrage
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Imagine working with cutting-edge machine learning models, crunching high frequency data sets and sparring with exceptional and fun colleagues, all while taking part in scaling our business even further.




Does this sound highly appealing to you? Then you might be our new Senior Quantitative Researcher in the Equity Statistical Arbitrage wing of Alipes Capital!




This position is focused on

Elevating our predictive modeling standards to the highest levels in the area of statistical arbitrage of traded funds.
Creating a world class modeling workflow, enabling the team to turn massive data sets of financial information into mathematical models that accurately predict movements in the markets.
In particular, the fixed-income section of our traded universe, in which we believe there is a significant untapped signal.




In doing so, you will get a chance to tackle a variety of software infrastructure challenges, such as:

Development and optimization of calibration and benchmarking frameworks.
Building out and implementing best practices for data preparation and dataset generation pipelines.
Prototyping and releasing novel predictive architectures, especially with respect to time-series models.




You will get instant validation of your work and experience short feedback cycles, where going from inception to deployment can be a matter of hours. There will be no red tape to cut and no sales people to consult. It is pure play.




About you

Fluency within mathematics and statistics.
Experience working with financial data, in particular valuation and hedging of fixed-income instruments.
Experience working with the full Machine Learning stack from data generation through model calibration and real-life validation and monitoring.
Programming experience with Python, in particular data-wrangling and numerical programming.
Proficiency with computer science fundamentals.
A scientific and inquisitive mind.




Nice to have

Experience working with ‘out-of-core’ datasets.
Experience working with tools like PyTorch, Tensorflow, XGBoost and/or Catboost.
Programming experience with languages like C# and C/C++.
PhD or MSc degree in engineering, physics, computer science, mathematics or economics.




About the team

At Alipes Capital, we have been a market leader in equity and electricity algorithmic trading since starting in 2008. We maintain an informal atmosphere where technical discussions are valued, and you are encouraged to take ownership of, and pride in, your work. You will impact the direction of the team, prioritize your work and choose the tools that get the job done.




The Quant team consists of eighteen passionate quantitative researchers covering 6 nationalities, with thirteen PhD’s and five MSc’s with expertise in statistical analysis, mathematical modeling and machine learning. The stat-arb sub-team is a tight group of 3 researchers.




We enjoy collaboration and are always willing to lend a helping hand. We work alongside a team of software engineers and a team of traders that implement and conceive the mathematical models together with us. All team members across the organization write code and drive change and are equally willing to engage on a nitty-gritty technical level as well as discuss the larger strategic level.




What we can offer you

Competitive benefits, including pension, health insurance, and 30 days of vacation.
A modern office in Copenhagen (Nordhavn) with a flexible hybrid work model.
A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions.
A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity.
Fast feedback and recognition of your contributions in a high-growth company.
Strong team spirit - successes are celebrated with company events and trips.




Practicalities

To apply, please send us your CV and a cover letter telling us why you think this role is a great fit for you. If your profile looks like a good match, we will get in touch to coordinate an online technical test as a first step in the interview process.

Title: Senior Associate - Data Science
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Senior Associate - Data Science

Consultant

Copenhagen · full time · permanent

This search is handled confidentially by Black Swans Exist. We name the company in the first conversation.




In short

You become the person the client calls. You own the relationship, you stand behind the delivery, and you build real depth in one field instead of being thrown between unrelated projects.

"Senior" here is about ownership, not years served. The sweet spot is two to five years of consulting experience.




About the company

We are recruiting for a Danish company in Copenhagen that builds and delivers software for the earliest stage of drug discovery.




When a pharmaceutical company develops a new drug, it has to decide which molecules are worth testing in the lab. The number of possibilities is effectively infinite. The lab can handle around a hundred.

This company builds the tools that find the right hundred — from choosing the target and the modality through to designing and screening the molecules.




The business model is a technology-driven consultancy. Their platform covers roughly 90% of the need out of the box, and the last 10% is built bespoke for each research project. That is why they deliver in a fraction of the time their competitors need.

They are around ten people, profitable, and the entire business has been built on referral. Their clients are pharma and biotech companies.




The role

The company has consultants who do the work at the client site, and a few more experienced people who own the client relationship itself. They need more of the second kind. That is you.

Title: PostDoc - Uncertainty-Aware Optimization in Inverse Problems for Next-Generation 3D Scanning
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
3Shape and DTU Compute (Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science at the Technical University of Denmark) invite applications for an Industrial Postdoctoral position partially funded by Innovation Fund Denmark. The position is a 2-year fixed-term appointment starting in January 2027 (small variations in the start date may be possible depending on the candidate’s preference).




The project addresses a fundamental challenge in computational imaging and large-scale optimization: how can uncertainty in measurements be quantified, propagated, and ultimately leveraged to improve the reliability of reconstructed 3d models?




Modern 3D scanning systems rely on advanced optimization algorithms to reconstruct geometry and color from large volumes of sensor data. While these algorithms produce highly accurate results, they typically provide limited information about the confidence and uncertainty associated with the reconstructed output. Developing methods that can efficiently estimate and propagate uncertainty in the input data through large-scale iterative optimization algorithms has the potential to improve reconstruction quality, enable more informed algorithmic decisions, and support the next generation of intelligent scanning systems.




The successful candidate will conduct research at the intersection of numerical linear algebra, optimization, uncertainty quantification, and computational imaging. The project will investigate: (i) how to characterize measurement uncertainty, (ii) how uncertainty propagates through iterative solvers, (iii) how to develop new mathematical frameworks for uncertainty-aware optimization, and (iv) how to validate the proposed methods through simulations and deployment in medical 3D reconstruction algorithms developed at 3Shape.




The position offers a unique opportunity to combine fundamental research with industrial impact. Working closely with leading researchers at DTU and engineers at 3Shape, the candidate will contribute to scientific publications, software prototype development, and innovation activities aimed at strengthening the theoretical foundations and practical performance of future 3D scanning technologies.




About us

At 3Shape we aim to advance dental treatment and diagnostics with advanced software and 3D scanners designed for dental professionals across the globe. Our purpose is to advance innovation in dentistry, continuously enhancing patient care and outcomes.




This role places you at the heart of our technological advancements within Product Creation, namely TRIOS & SCANNER SW, offering the chance to shape the trajectory of our innovative products and software applications.




About the project

The project is a 2-year project between 3Shape and the Technical University of Denmark, partly funded by Innovation Fund Denmark. The academic co-supervisor will be Professor Per Christian Hansen at DTU Compute (Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science).




The research focuses on uncertainty-aware methods for large-scale linear least squares problems, which form the mathematical backbone of many inverse problems and optimization tasks in 3D reconstruction. The objective is to develop new theoretical and computational tools for quantifying and propagating uncertainty through iterative solution methods, and to translate these developments into practical algorithms for medical 3D reconstruction systems.




What You’ll Do

In this role, you will contribute both to the theoretical foundation and the practical implementation of next-generation uncertainty-aware reconstruction algorithms. The work spans mathematical modelling, algorithm design, and software development in a medical imaging 3D reconstruction.

You will:

Develop methods for characterizing measurement uncertainty in medical 3D scanning data, including data-driven approaches and machine learning methods where appropriate, to obtain realistic and application-relevant uncertainty models.
Work hands-on with numerical algorithms, including iterative methods such as Krylov subspace methods and related solvers.
Develop and analyse new methods for uncertainty-aware linear least squares optimization, with a focus on large-scale iterative solvers.
Design mathematical frameworks for quantifying how uncertainty evolves through optimization algorithms used in 3D reconstruction.
Contribute to the architectural design of uncertainty-aware components within existing reconstruction pipelines.
Translate theoretical models into efficient, scalable implementations suitable for industrial use.
Design and run simulation studies to validate theoretical developments under realistic conditions.
Collaborate with researchers and engineers to integrate new methods into production-oriented 3D scanning systems.
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, technical reports, and potential patentable innovations.




What We’re Looking For

A PhD in Mathematics, Statistics, or a related discipline. The PhD must have been awarded after March 2021 (or will be obtained within November 2026).
Strong expertise in numerical linear algebra, optimization, and/or inverse problems.
Solid understanding of linear least squares methods and iterative solvers, ideally methods based on Krylov subspace methods.
Experience with or strong interest in uncertainty quantification, statistical modelling, or probabilistic methods.
Strong programming skills in at least one programming language (ideally two), such as C#, C++, or Python.
Familiarity with machine learning methods is an advantage, particularly for data-driven modelling of complex systems.
Ability to work independently and take ownership of research problems while also contributing to a collaborative industrial-academic environment.
Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex mathematical ideas clearly in both academic and applied settings.




What 3Shape offers

A vibrant and international environment with social, diverse, and highly skilled and collaborative colleagues - we are more than 50 nationalities in our DK based office
Breakfast every day, and delicious and healthy lunch cooked by our private chefs.
We provide a great social work environment with many optional activities and social clubs, ranging from wine & beer, board games, running to bicycle clubs.
Good work/life balance.
Attractive offices and R&D lab spaces in downtown Copenhagen close to Kgs. Nytorv, Nyhavn, and the Copenhagen Canals.
Purpose: Endeavor to improve dental patients on a global scale.




Staying true to our values and D&I efforts, we encourage all relevant applicants to apply, and we ask you NOT to add any photos or sensitive information (age, marital status, nationality) during the application process.




We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

Title: Scientist, Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology (PK/PD Modeling & Simulation)
Description:
Join Hemab, a clinical-stage biotech company, on an exciting journey to build the ultimate clotting company. We focus on addressing the high unmet needs of patients suffering from rare bleeding and thrombotic disorders. With offices in Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark, Hemab cultivates a vibrant, agile and forward-thinking environment where collaboration, innovation, and high-quality biotherapeutics development go hand in hand.

As a Scientist, PK/PD Modeling & Simulation, you will be responsible for developing, validating, and applying population PK, PK/PD, exposure–response and QSP models to support model-informed drug development across Hemab’s pipeline. You will work closely with internal cross-functional leads (clinical pharmacology, nonclinical, clinical development, biometrics, regulatory and quality) and external collaborators (CROs and consultants) to provide quantitative insights that inform dose selection, clinical study design, and regulatory filings. Your work will be central to integrating modeling and simulation strategies into Hemab’s clinical programs and advancing our mission to deliver first-in-class therapies to patients with rare bleeding disorders.

At Hemab, we foster an environment where everyone can wear multiple hats depending on their experience, fit, and motivation to get things done. We constantly strive to celebrate our achievements collectively and gather feedback to continuously sustain and improve our fast-paced, cross-functional work environment.




What you'll do at Hemab?

Develop, validate, and execute population PK, PK/PD exposure–response, PBPK and QSP models to support dose selection, regimen optimization, and trial design.
Perform simulations to inform early clinical study design, establish clinical proof-of-concept (PoC), and guide pivotal program decisions.
Analyze preclinical and clinical PK/PD data, translating insights into actionable recommendations for clinical teams.
Contribute quantitative components for regulatory submissions (INDs, CTAs, BLAs) and respond to agency questions on modeling and simulation deliverables.
Collaborate cross-functionally to ensure modeling insights are integrated into development plans and communicated clearly to stakeholders.
Stay current with regulatory expectations, industry trends, and new quantitative methods to continuously improve modeling strategies and workflows.
Support vendor and consultant selection and management to ensure high-quality, timely deliverables for modeling and simulation activities.
Be a proactive and collaborative team player, receptive to constructive feedback and committed to meeting program goals.




Who You Are and What You'll Bring to Hemab?

Education: Ph.D. in Pharmacometrics, Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacokinetics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or related field; with 1–3 years of relevant experience.
Experience: Hands-on experience with population PK/PD modeling software (NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix NLME) and programming languages (R, MATLAB). Strong understanding of PK/PD principles, biologics drug development, and model-informed drug development strategies.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred: biologics PK/PD, rare disease development, translational modeling, or target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD). Familiarity with quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) approaches is a plus.
Demonstrated ability to analyze, interpret, and communicate complex quantitative data to diverse audiences, including cross-functional teams and regulatory authorities.
Experience contributing to or supporting regulatory submissions is desirable.
Excellent problem-solving skills, scientific curiosity, and the ability to thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced biotech environment.

Title: AI Engineer - On-site Copenhagen
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
AI Engineer

AI is moving from prototypes to production-ready solutions. The engineers who can take it there matter more than ever.

At Heyra, we build operational AI: systems, workflows, and data platforms that live in production from day one. We work with companies that are moving quickly and need solutions that improve the way they operate.

We're looking for an AI Engineer who is as comfortable in the code as in the data underneath it. Someone who can design, build, and ship AI solutions today, and grow into setting technical direction as the company grows.

On smaller engagements, you may be the only engineer on the project, which means owning it from problem to production yourself. On larger ones, you'll work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists, and designers in a company where ideas move quickly, and the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

What you'll work on


Designing and deploying AI solutions across domains like finance, operations, and supply chain
Building predictive models, automated workflows, and agentic systems
Owning the data work behind your own models and agents
Building eval systems that measure whether an agent actually works
Leading client projects from problem to production
Translating business needs into AI solutions that actually ship
Integrating scalable AI systems through APIs and cloud environments


Requirements

You probably have experience with


Software development, ML or data engineering, with AI applications running in production
Fluent Python and at least one agent framework or SDK
Training ML models and handling the data preparation behind them
Building or extending eval systems for agent behaviour
Building scalable systems in cloud environments like Azure or GCP
Coding with agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
Stakeholder management and leading delivery end-to-end


Curiosity, taste and builder mentality matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience.

Why Heyra

We believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We are building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build and operate AI products that change how enterprises work, from problem to prototype to production.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high. We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

People here care about what they build. Good ideas move quickly. New technology gets explored early. There is room to shape both the company and the way we work.

We are around 45 people today, and we are only just getting started.

If this sounds like your kind of work, send us a short note about yourself together with your CV. We care much more about curiosity, energy and the way you think than polished applications.

Benefits


Healthcare insurance
Pension plan
Parental leave
Social gatherings
New tech gear
Central office
Free lunch, coffee, snacks, and Friday beers
Skill development
Paid holiday
Remote work allowed
Pet friendly

Vil du arbejde med kvantitativ analyse fra den indledende problemstilling til den endelige anbefaling? Og motiveres du af at bruge data til at skabe et klart beslutningsgrundlag for kunder?

Vi søger en Data Insights Consultant til vores team i København eller Aarhus.

Hos Wilke arbejder du med både private og offentlige kunder på projekter, hvor analyse skal omsættes til konkrete forretningsmæssige beslutninger. Det kan eksempelvis være evaluering af kundestrategier, segmentering, brandpositionering, konceptudvikling, produkt- og pristests eller andre skræddersyede analyser.

Som Data Insights Consultant vil du


Indgå i projektteams og være med til at definere den analytiske tilgang til kundens problemstilling
Udarbejde spørgeskemaer og sikre, at undersøgelsesdesignet understøtter det spørgsmål, analysen skal besvare
Arbejde med databehandling, kvantitativ analyse og fortolkning af resultater
Udarbejde rapporter, præsentationer, konklusioner og anbefalinger
Have direkte dialog med kunder og deltage i kundemøder sammen med den kundeansvarlige
Rådgive kunder med udgangspunkt i data og deres forretningsmæssige behov
Have ansvar for egne projekter og sikre fremdrift, kvalitet og deadlines


Du får mulighed for at arbejde bredt med forskellige typer analyser og kunder og samtidig udvikle dine kompetencer inden for både analyse og rådgivning. Vi lægger vægt på faglig sparring og på, at man hjælper hinanden på tværs af projekter og kompetencer.

Hvem er du?

Vi Forestiller Os, At Du


Har minimum 3 års erfaring som analytiker, eksempelvis fra et analyseinstitut, mediebureau, konsulenthus eller en analyseafdeling
Har en relevant kandidatuddannelse, f.eks. cand.merc., cand.oecon., cand.scient.pol., cand.merc.(mat.) eller tilsvarende
Har en stærk kvantitativ profil og solid erfaring med statistiske analysemetoder
Har erfaring med R, SPSS, Q eller tilsvarende analyse- og databehandlingsværktøjer
Er vant til at arbejde med komplekse datasæt og kan identificere de vigtigste mønstre og sammenhænge i data
Kan formidle analytiske resultater klart og præcist – både skriftligt og mundtligt på dansk og engelsk
Arbejder struktureret og har blik for både detaljer og det overordnede formål med analysen
Kan drive egne opgaver og projekter, men samtidig trives med tæt samarbejde i et team
Har lyst til at være i dialog med kunder og omsætte analyse til anbefalinger, der kan bruges i praksis


Det vigtigste er ikke, at du kan alle metoder på forhånd. Vi søger en stærk analytiker, der kan forstå en problemstilling, vælge den rigtige tilgang og formidle resultatet, så det giver mening for modtageren.

Hvem er Wilke?

Wilke er en dansk rådgivnings- og analysevirksomhed, der hjælper virksomheder og organisationer med at træffe bedre beslutninger gennem data, analyse og rådgivning.

Vi arbejder med nogle af Danmarks største virksomheder og organisationer og løser både faste analyseopgaver og mere komplekse, skræddersyede problemstillinger.

Vi har kontorer i København, Aarhus og Odense og lægger vægt på et stærkt fagligt miljø, hvor man arbejder tæt sammen på tværs af teams. Du får en fleksibel arbejdsdag med mulighed for hjemmearbejde, men vi ser kontoret som et vigtigt sted for faglig sparring og samarbejde.

Det sociale fællesskab er også en vigtig del af Wilke. Vi vil gerne være en arbejdsplads, hvor man føler sig godt tilpas og som en del af holdet – uanset om man trives bedst med den gode faglige samtale over en kop kaffe, fælles aktiviteter med de nærmeste kolleger eller større arrangementer på tværs af organisationen. I løbet af året har vi derfor både lokale aktiviteter på vores tre kontorer og fælles arrangementer, hvor kolleger fra hele Wilke mødes. Det vigtigste for os er, at du har lyst til at bidrage til et fagligt stærkt og inkluderende fællesskab, hvor der er plads til forskellige personligheder, perspektiver og måder at arbejde på.

Interesseret?

Hvis du kan se dig selv i rollen som Data Insights Consultant hos Wilke i København eller Aarhus, så send os dit CV og en ansøgning.

Yderligere oplysninger om stillingen fås hos Philip Nørskov Alexandersen, Head of Data Insights, på PNA@wilke.dk eller +45 51 64 02 93.

Vi holder samtaler løbende. Tiltrædelse efter aftale. Læs mere om Wilke på wilke.dk.

Title: Open Talent Pool - all DHI locations
Place: Hørsholm, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
At DHI, water, environment and sustainability meet innovation. Join us in enabling a sustainable future for water!

Looking to make an impact on our planet? At DHI, you can. We work with water in all its forms – combining deep domain knowledge, advanced digital technology, and more than 60 years of research and innovation to help society use, manage and live with water sustainably. With over 1,100 engineers and specialists across 26 countries, we are continually expanding our global community of experts.

As we grow, new opportunities emerge throughout the year. Even when a specific vacancy isn’t yet published, we welcome proactive applications from individuals who want to contribute to our mission – including senior specialist with years of experience or students, recent graduates and early career professionals who are excited to build their future in the water sector.

Why submit an open application?

Our business evolves quickly, and new roles – technical, scientific, digital and business-oriented – are created as projects grow and priorities shift. Submitting an open application adds you to our Open Talent Pool, enabling us to reach out when a suitable opportunity arises, often before it is advertised.

Before you submit your open application, please make sure to check our current vacancies as well.

Opportunities for Students & Early Career Talent

We strongly encourage students and early career professionals to apply.

At DHI, You Can


Join as an intern, student assistant, thesis collaboration partner or industry master program student
Contribute to global water projects alongside experienced specialists
Apply your academic knowledge to real-world environmental and digital challenges
Grow your skills in engineering, modelling, climate resilience, data science, software development, sustainability and more
Work in a culture that supports experimentation, learning and exploration


If you are studying or recently graduated in engineering, environmental science, climate studies, digital technology, or related fields – and want to help shape a sustainable future – your application is very welcome.

Profiles we are interested in

We invite applications from experienced professionals, graduates, and students with interest or expertise in:


Engineering & Environmental Science Coastal, marine, environmental, hydraulic, climate, civil, ecosystem modelling
Data, Digital & Technology Software development, data science, machine learning, AI, digital product development
Consulting & Project Delivery Advisory services, modelling, client engagement, project/programme management
Sustainability & ESG
Corporate Functions Legal, compliance, HR, finance, operations, commercial roles


We value cross disciplinary thinkers—if your background doesn’t fit into a category, we still encourage you to apply.

What We Offer

When you join DHI, you are empowered to be an explorer—to innovate, collaborate, and continuously learn. You’ll be part of a global organisation committed to protecting water ecosystems and developing sustainable solutions for communities, cities, industries and the planet.

Positions May Be


Fulltime or parttime
Based in various global locations or open to flexible arrangements
Project based or permanent, depending on organisational needs


How To Apply


Please submit your application through our careers page under “Open Talent”. If you are interested in other locations, please indicate that clearly.


Kindly Attach


Your CV
A brief note outlining your area of interests, skills and how you found DHI
List your preferred DHI location(s)
Links to portfolio, publications, or project work (optional)


Learn more about DHI www.dhigroup.com

Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark

Are you motivated by working with data, analytics, and quantitative problem-solving in the financial services sector? Do you have 1–4 years of experience from banking, consultancy, or a similar data-driven environment, and would you like to help clients turn complex data into clear insights and practical solutions? Welcome to KPMG.

We are looking for a curious and structured data and analytical profile to join our Financial Services Advisory team. As a Consultant or Senior Consultant at KPMG, you will support banks and financial institutions with data analysis, quantitative assessments, reporting, regulatory data requirements, and the development of practical analytics solutions. The role is ideal for someone with a solid analytical foundation, hands-on data skills, and an interest in how data supports business decisions, performance management, risk management, and regulatory compliance.

About The Position

As our new colleague in Financial Services Advisory, you will work with data and quantitative assignments across banking and financial services, including opportunities to:


Support clients with data analysis, data quality assessments, reporting, and analytical insights across banking and financial services.
Contribute to the development, validation, and implementation of credit risk methodologies and models (PD, LGD, CCF), including segmentation, calibration, parameter estimation, performance monitoring, model governance, and regulatory compliance within IRB and risk management frameworks.
Transform, structure, and automate large and complex datasets from banking processes, customer portfolios, finance, risk, loss databases, and regulatory reporting.
Support projects related to data governance, BCBS 239, data lineage, controls, documentation, and management reporting.
Develop analyses, dashboards, and quantitative solutions using tools such as SQL, Python, SAS, Excel, and Power BI.
Translate complex data findings into clear conclusions, recommendations, and client-ready presentations.
Participate in client meetings, proposals, and internal development initiatives as part of a collaborative advisory team.


You will gain exposure to a broad range of data-driven projects and build a solid consulting toolkit while developing your technical, analytical, and communication skills in a financial services context.

The ideal candidate

The ideal candidate is a motivated professional who enjoys working with data, solving problems, and communicating insights clearly. We imagine that you bring:


A master’s degree in a quantitative or data-related field, such as economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, actuarial, engineering, computer science, or similar discipline.
Approximately 1–4 years of relevant experience from a bank, financial institution, consultancy, or data/analytics function.
Hands-on experience working with data extraction, data preparation, data quality, analysis, reporting, or dashboarding.
Solid analytical skills and the ability to structure complex problems, identify patterns, and draw practical conclusions.
Experience with SQL, Python, SAS, Excel, Power BI, or similar tools. Experience with credit risk modelling, IRB methodologies, IFRS 9, model monitoring, banking data and products, BCBS 239, regulatory reporting, or data governance.
The ability to communicate clearly in English, both verbally and in writing, and to present data-driven insights in a simple and client-oriented way.


This is an opportunity to grow as a data and quantitative consultant, working closely with experienced colleagues and clients on assignments where high-quality data, sound analysis, and clear communication make a real difference.

This position involves limited international travel activities. You’re working address will be at Dampfærgevej 28, 2100 Copenhagen and at the client’s site. We offer flexible work-from-home opportunities but prioritize meetings at the office on Fridays to be with colleagues.

Why KPMG?

KPMG offers a competitive compensation package, healthcare, fitness, sports clubs, massage on-site, fruit, and canteen facilities.

You’ll thrive in a professional environment that emphasizes close team collaboration and cross-functional, international partnerships. You won’t just be a part of a team; You will become integral to a motivated and skilled team of over 60 international professionals focused on progression and professional development.

Our culture is not just a buzzword – It is social, informal, and open, with a flat organizational structure. We value diversity, social well-being, collaboration, and innovative thinking.

Ready to work on data-driven financial services?

Apply now to be part of a collaborative team where your skills are not just valued – It is celebrated!

If you find yourself aligned with this opportunity, then we would like to get to know you better.

Feel free to contact Claus Bruhn Bentzen, cbentzen@kpmg.com or Bjørn Larsen, bjolarsen@kpmg.com . We accept applications and interview candidates continuously and will close the position once we have found the right match.

At KPMG, we are committed to developing diverse talents at all levels. We encourage all interested candidates to apply, regardless of age, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or ethnicity.

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
We are looking for a Core Data Scientist to apply ML, statistical modelling and experimentation to solve complex business problems and drive measurable outcomes across our client base. You will work hands-on with large datasets, developing and deploying models, running tests and translating data into clear, actionable insights.

The role focuses on building scalable data science solutions, validating performance through experimentation and partnering with stakeholders to ensure analytical outputs deliver real business impact.

About Us

Optima Partners is a fast‑growing professional services firm helping leading organisations transform customer engagement at the intersection of marketing, technology and data. We work with major brands including Lloyds Banking Group, NatWest, Nationwide, Aviva, Virgin Media O2, BT, Centrica, and GSK. As we scale from 80 to 200 people we’re growing our Advanced Data team.

We are collaborative, curious and focused on delivering practical insight that helps organisations make better decisions and grow sustainably. You will join a practitioner-led business with a strong data science community, working alongside people who are passionate about applying analytical thinking to real-world business problems.

About The Role

As a Core Data Scientist, you will be a technical specialist who develops and implements ML models that deliver meaningful value for our clients. You will work closely with stakeholders to understand business challenges, translate requirements into analytical solutions, and turn complex outputs into clear, actionable insight.

This is a great opportunity for a passionate data scientist to build their career across multiple commercial sectors, contribute to multi-disciplinary project teams and play an active role in a growing data science practice.

What You Will Be Doing


Developing and implementing machine learning and statistical models to solve practical business problems
Working with stakeholders to understand objectives, shape analytical approaches, and communicate findings effectively
Translating technical outputs into clear, transparent, and actionable recommendations to support decision-making
Exploring data, testing hypotheses, and identifying opportunities to create customer and commercial value
Collaborating with teams across data science, engineering, strategy, and design to deliver high-quality outcomes
Keeping up to date with emerging data science techniques, including practical applications of Large Language Models


What We Would Like You To Have


Strong academic background in mathematics, statistics, science, engineering, or another numerate discipline
Minimum 2:1 degree in a STEM subject, with a postgraduate qualification in a quantitative field considered beneficial
Good knowledge of statistics, including experimental design, uncertainty quantification, and predictive modelling
Experience with supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques, ideally in a commercial environment
Proficiency in Python and/or R, with the ability to quickly learn new tools and approaches to operationalising data science solutions
Ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to audiences with both technical and non-technical backgrounds
Inquisitive mindset, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to work independently or as part of a small team
Awareness of commercial value drivers such as revenue, cost, profitability, and customer behaviour is advantageous
A strong academic background in maths, statistics, science, engineering or another numerate discipline.


Why join us

At Optima, you will work on varied, meaningful projects for well-known organisations while continuing to develop your technical expertise. You will be part of a supportive data science community with a strong culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing and collaboration.

You will have the opportunity to apply your skills across different sectors, learn from experienced practitioners and build a career path with clear opportunities for development and progression.

What’s on offer


Competitive salary + bonus up to 15%
37 days holiday (incl. Christmas shutdown)
Private medical insurance, life & income protection
Pension scheme
1,000+ employee perks
Dedicated learning, training, and certification support


If you’re ready to build your career in a practitioner-led consultancy where data science is applied to meaningful, real-world problems, we’d love to hear from you.

Title: Senior Data Scientist
Description:
At 1st Central, everything starts with our people.




As one of the UK’s leading motor and home insurers, we use smart technology, data and great service to make insurance fast, fair and simple for over 1.4 million customers. We’re proud to create an environment where people feel supported, trusted and able to grow - whether that’s developing new skills, taking on fresh challenges or making a real impact every day. If you’re looking for a role where you can make a difference, we’d love to hear from you.




We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join a high-performing team focused on turning complex data into actionable insights, delivering innovative solutions that drive business value and support strategic decision-making.




In this role, you’ll work both independently and collaboratively to apply data science techniques that drive meaningful outcomes. You’ll work with large and diverse datasets from multiple sources, spanning both structured and unstructured formats. Using strong critical‑thinking and problem‑solving skills, you’ll analyse and interpret data, build predictive models, and develop machine learning algorithms that generate actionable insights.




You’ll propose solutions to business challenges and collaborate with other teams to implement them. Recognising the dependencies Group companies have on in‑house technology, the Senior Data Scientist will work closely and seamlessly with the Group’s in-house technology provider, along with data presentation/delivery teams based across multiple locations.




We’re big on flexible hybrid working. Our teams are based across Haywards Heath (West Sussex) and Salford Quays (Manchester). We primarily work from home but value collaboration, so we come together in person to keep ideas flowing, typically once a quarter. Prefer being in the office more often? That works for us too.




Core skills we’re looking for to succeed in the role:




Professional Experience: Proven experience in a Data Science role, delivering data-driven solutions and insights to support business decision making. Insurance industry experience is highly advantageous but not essential
Analytical & Technical Expertise: Strong analytical capability, with proven experience in statistical modelling skills, and data interpretation
Technical Skills: Proficiency in Python for data analysis, modelling and machine learning.
Machine Learning: Experience building and evaluating machine learning models
Education: Degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, or another quantitative field
Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills
Organisation & Time Management: Excellent organisational and time management skills

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
Role Requirements

We are seeking a pragmatic and skilled Data Scientist to join The Product Counsel team, working remotely with a preference for candidates based in London or Cambridge. In this role, you'll harness the power of vast advertising datasets to develop, evaluate, and deploy machine learning models that drive real business impact. You'll collaborate closely with a dedicated data engineer, allowing you to focus on modelling, mathematics, and delivering actionable insights—but if you’re eager to get hands-on across the stack, we encourage and support that, too!

What You’ll Do

Analyze large-scale advertising datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and actionable insights


Select, train, and evaluate machine learning models tailored to business and performance outcomes
Leverage Python (and PyTorch) in notebooks to extract, explore, and model data
Collaborate with engineers to hand off models and support production deployment
Translate model outputs into clear, actionable business intelligence for stakeholders
Optionally: Get hands-on with data engineering tasks (pipelines, ETL, infrastructure) if desired


What We’re Looking For

Strong background in data science, statistics, and machine learning


Hands-on experience with Python and PyTorch
Proficient with large datasets, ideally on GCP (Google Cloud Platform) and BigQuery
Comfortable working in notebooks and writing reproducible, clear code
Experience with advertising or marketing data (ideal, but not required)
Experience working at an SSP (Supply Side Platform), DSP (Demand Side Platform), or DMP (Data Management Platform) is highly desirable. These platforms are integral to the digital advertising ecosystem, enabling automated buying, selling, and management of ad inventory and data
Bonus: Data engineering skills (pipelines, infrastructure, ETL) and an interest in using them
Able to work independently and communicate complex ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences


Location & Benefits

Remote role with a preference for candidates based in London or Cambridge


Flexible working hours and a collaborative, supportive team culture
Opportunity to work on impactful, high-visibility projects in the advertising technology space

This role is about progressing the adoption of data-driven methods, machine learning and AI more widely within the business. You will work with a range of colleagues and teams to help solve complex business problems, unlock business insight and value from semi-structured and structured data, support data-driven decision-making and develop new data products and models. Gather feedback and monitor the continued performance and accuracy of outputs, including ML models, as applicable.
Build understanding of Registers of Scotland data, business processes, strategic objectives and the policy environment in which we operate.
Draw on government and industry technical/analytical standards and frameworks and adhere to the UK Government data ethics framework.
Communicate insights and results to technical and non-technical audiences using presentations, data visualisation and data storytelling.
Build awareness of technical, regulatory and social developments in industry.
Support development of the team by participating in strategy development, communities of practice, staff management and team capability building.

Work with purpose: we strive to provide the best public service and set the bar for land and property registration worldwide.
Flexible and hybrid working:, work when and where it’s best for you and your stakeholders, depending on the role and team requirements.

Positive work culture: RoS is an agile, digital organisation using leading-edge technology. Colleagues understand their role in achieving our strategy and have the autonomy to deliver.




To learn more about RoS and the benefits we offer visit our careers pages or watch this short video.




Hear directly from our colleagues about their experience of working within our Digital, Data and Technology teams on our website.

Backend: Java, Python and Spring Boots
Frontend: JavaScript, React and Typescript

AWS: AWS SNS, Comprehend, EC2, Lambdas, RDS, SageMaker and Textract

Title: Senior Data Scientist
Description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to lead the design and delivery of machine learning, statistical modelling and experimentation solutions that solve complex business problems and drive measurable outcomes across our client base. You will combine hands-on technical expertise with strong consulting and stakeholder skills, shaping analytical approaches, guiding delivery and translating data into clear, actionable insight.

The role focuses on developing scalable data science solutions, validating performance through robust experimentation, leading technical decision-making and partnering with senior stakeholders to ensure analytical outputs deliver real commercial impact.

About Us

Optima Partners is a fast‑growing professional services firm helping leading organisations transform customer engagement at the intersection of marketing, technology and data. We work with major brands including Lloyds Banking Group, NatWest, Nationwide, Aviva, Virgin Media O2, BT, Centrica, and GSK. As we scale from 80 to 200 people we’re growing our Advanced Data team.

We are collaborative, curious and focused on delivering practical insight that helps organisations make better decisions and grow sustainably. You will join a practitioner-led business with a strong data science community, working alongside people who are passionate about applying analytical thinking to real-world business problems.

About The Role

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will be a technical lead responsible for shaping, developing and implementing machine learning and statistical solutions that deliver meaningful value for our clients. You will work closely with senior stakeholders to understand business challenges, define analytical strategies, oversee delivery and turn complex outputs into clear, actionable recommendations.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced data scientist to take ownership of high-impact work across multiple commercial sectors, contribute to multi-disciplinary project teams and play a visible role in growing and developing our data science practice.

What You Will Be Doing


Leading the development and implementation of machine learning and statistical models to solve practical, high-value business problems
Partnering with senior stakeholders to understand objectives, shape analytical approaches, influence decisions and communicate findings effectively
Translating complex technical outputs into clear, transparent and actionable recommendations that support strategic decision-making
Exploring data, testing hypotheses and identifying opportunities to create customer, operational and commercial value
Collaborating with and guiding teams across data science, engineering, strategy and design to deliver high-quality outcomes
Championing emerging data science techniques, including practical applications of Large Language Models, and helping translate them into client-ready solutions
Mentoring junior colleagues, reviewing analytical work and contributing to the development of best practice within the Advanced Data team


What We Would Like You To Have


Strong academic background in mathematics, statistics, science, engineering or another numerate discipline
Minimum 2:1 degree in a STEM subject, with a postgraduate qualification in a quantitative field considered beneficial
Deep knowledge of statistics, including experimental design, uncertainty quantification, causal inference and predictive modelling
Significant experience applying supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques in commercial or client-facing environments
Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R, with experience operationalising data science solutions and working with modern data science tooling
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex analysis clearly and confidently to technical and non-technical audiences
Strong problem-solving skills, commercial curiosity and the ability to lead work independently while supporting others in small, high-performing teams
Strong understanding of commercial value drivers such as revenue, cost, profitability, customer behaviour and operational performance
Experience mentoring junior data scientists, reviewing analytical approaches and contributing to technical standards or reusable assets


Why join us

At Optima, you will work on varied, meaningful projects for well-known organisations while continuing to deepen your technical expertise and leadership capability. You will be part of a supportive data science community with a strong culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing and collaboration.

You will have the opportunity to shape analytical solutions across different sectors, learn from experienced practitioners, mentor others and build a career path with clear opportunities for senior development and progression.

What’s On Offer


Competitive salary + bonus up to 15%
37 days holiday (incl. Christmas shutdown)
Private medical insurance, life & income protection
Pension scheme
1,000+ employee perks
Dedicated learning, training, and certification support


If you’re ready to take a senior role in a practitioner-led consultancy where data science is applied to meaningful, real-world problems, we’d love to hear from you.

Title: Senior Data Scientist
Description:
Help transform the future of British Army training through the power of data.

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist who has applied data science in the real world, working with stakeholders to solve meaningful business or operational challenges, not just building models in isolation.

Technical skills matter, but we're equally interested in how you think, collaborate and approach problems.

Job Title

Senior Data Scientist

Job Description

🕒 Permanent role - 37.5 hours a week

📍 Hybrid role with 2 or 3 days a week in Warminster

🔐 Due to the nature of this role, you must be eligible for UK Security Clearance at BPSS level.

What You’ll Be Doing


Work directly with stakeholders to understand problems, challenge assumptions and identify opportunities.
Turn complex operational questions into practical data science solutions.
Apply analytics, statistics and machine learning to generate meaningful insights and recommendations.
Build models, analytical products and visualisations that support decision-making.
Communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Collaborate across multidisciplinary teams while retaining the freedom to explore problems in depth.
Operate confidently in environments where the answer is not always obvious.
Champion evidence-based decision-making and help grow a culture of curiosity, learning and continuous improvement.


What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who:


Is naturally curious and enjoys tackling difficult real-world challenges.
Has experience with complex, large-scale data in mission critical contexts.
Wants to understand the people, processes and decisions behind the data.
Has experience applying data science to solve genuine business or operational problems.
Can build credibility with stakeholders and communicate complex ideas simply.
Is comfortable working independently, taking ownership and navigating ambiguity.
Enjoys collaborating with others and contributing to a supportive, high-performing team.
Can move comfortably between stakeholder conversations and hands-on technical work.
Is motivated by delivering measurable outcomes rather than building models for their own sake.
Enjoys testing a hypothesis, iteration, experimentation and prototyping
Can comfortably translate results in non-technical language, while being also able to defend the maths behind the models


Essential Skills/Experience/Qualifications


Strong practical experience in data science, statistics or advanced analytics.
Experience using Python, R, SQL and relevant analytical or machine learning techniques.
A track record of translating analytical findings into actionable recommendations and decisions.


Desirable Skills/Experience/Qualifications


Knowledge and experience of collective training
Knowledge of the military/Army


About ACTS (Army Collective Training Service)

The OMNIA® Training consortium brings together five leading UK defence training organisations: Capita, Raytheon, Rheinmetall, Cervus and Skyral. As the British Army’s Strategic Training Partner (STP), OMNIA has a clear mission: to transform collective training over the next 15 years and deliver world-class training for the British Army.

Working with the Land Warfare Centre (LWC), OMNIA will schedule, plan, design, deliver and assure collective training across the Army’s Collective Training System (ACTS), while also delivering the Collective Training Transformation Programme (CTTP). This generational opportunity will enable more relevant, challenging and safe training, helping the British Army to fight and win. Central to this mission is the ability to set and measure training performance against requirements, assure operational readiness, and capture associated training and safety risks.

What’s in it for you?


Salary up to £60,000 depending on skills and experience
Enjoy flexible benefits including extra leave purchase, paid volunteering days, enhanced family leave, lifestyle discounts, and access to inclusive employee networks — all designed to support your wellbeing and personal growth.
Onsite, secure parking
Rewarding role making a real difference to those joining and progressing within the British Army
Flexible working
